statement.name: Halpern–Läuchli theorem
statement.definition: For infinite leafless trees T_0..T_{d-1} and a k-coloring of the level products ⋃_n T_0(n)×…×T_{d-1}(n), there are strong subtrees with a common level function whose level product is monochromatic.
statement.facts: It is computably true (Theorem 3.4), its forest version is computably true (Theorem 3.6), and it admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 3.21).

statement.name: Milliken's tree theorem for height 1
statement.definition: Milliken's tree theorem restricted to colorings of strong subtrees of height 1 (i.e. nodes).
statement.facts: It admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 3.13).

statement.name: Product version of Milliken's tree theorem for height n
statement.definition: For d infinite leafless trees and a k-coloring of S_n(T_0,…,T_{d-1}), there is a tuple in S_ω(T_0,…,T_{d-1}) on which the coloring is constant.
statement.facts: Every X-computable instance has a Δ^{0,X}_{2n-1} solution (Theorem 4.6). It is provable in ACA0, and (∀n)PMTT^n is provable in ACA'_0 (Corollary 4.7). PMTT^n is equivalent to ACA0 for n≥3 and (∀n)PMTT^n is equivalent to ACA'_0 (Corollary 4.9). PMTT^2 admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Theorem 4.15, Corollary 4.16).

statement.name: Product Milliken tree theorem with ℓ colors allowed in the solution
statement.definition: Like PMTT^n with k colors, but the solution may take at most ℓ colors.
statement.facts: PMTT^2_{k,2} admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 4.27). (∀k)PMTT^3_{k,2} admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Theorem 4.28, Corollary 4.29). It implies (∀k)JDT^2_{k,4} (Theorem 5.43).

statement.name: Ramsey's theorem with ℓ colors allowed in the solution
statement.definition: Every f:[N]^n→k has an infinite H such that f uses at most ℓ colors on [H]^n.
statement.facts: Strong cone avoidance of RT^2_{k,2} is cited from Wang and Cholak–Patey. RT^2_{k,ℓ} ≤_c DT^2_{2k,2ℓ+1} (Theorem 5.32). JRG^2_{4k,4n+3} implies RT^2_{k,n} (Theorem 6.41).

statement.name: Devlin's theorem
statement.definition: Every f:[Q]^n→k has a dense suborder S without endpoints with |f([S]^n)| ≤ ℓ.
statement.facts: There is a computable instance of DT^2_{4,3} all of whose solutions compute ∅' (Theorem 5.28), so DT^2_{4,3} implies ACA0 (Corollary 5.31). RT^2_{k,ℓ} ≤_c DT^2_{2k,2ℓ+1} (Theorem 5.32). (∀k)DT^2_{k,ℓ} has a computable instance whose solutions are all DNC relative to ∅'' and none of which is Σ^0_3 (Corollaries 5.39, 5.41). DT^2_{4,2} implies ER^2 (Theorem 5.48). DT^2_{<∞,4} (via JDT) admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Corollaries 5.44, 5.45). Tight bounds are the odd tangent numbers (Corollary 5.26).

statement.name: Joyce Devlin's theorem
statement.definition: Devlin's theorem for DLO Joyce structures: there is a substructure copy on which f uses at most ℓ colors.
statement.facts: It is equivalent to DT for the same parameters (Corollary 5.25, Corollary 5.8). (∀k)PMTT^3_{k,2} implies (∀k)JDT^2_{k,4} (Theorem 5.43). (∀k)JDT^2_{k,4} admits cone avoidance (Corollary 5.44).

statement.name: Rado graph theorem
statement.definition: Every k-coloring of n-subsets (or of copies of G) of the Rado graph has a Rado subgraph on which at most ℓ colors appear.
statement.facts: (∀k)RG^2_{k,4} admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Theorem 6.32, Corollary 6.40). For F of size 3 with b the number of Joyce types of F, (∀k)RG^F_{k,b} implies ACA0 (Corollary 6.48, Theorem 6.45, PA over ∅'). (∀k)RG^{K_3}_{k,16} and (∀k)RG^3_{k,112} imply ACA0 (Corollaries 6.49, 6.51). RG^2_{8,4} implies SRT^2_2 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.55). RT^2_2 does not imply (∀k)RG^2_{k,ℓ} for any ℓ (Theorem 6.63, via an ω-model).

statement.name: Joyce Rado graph theorem
statement.definition: Rado graph theorem for Joyce Rado graph structures.
statement.facts: Tight bound is the number of Joyce graphs (Corollary 6.27, ACA0). JRG^2_{4k,4n+3} implies RT^2_{k,n} and JRG^2_{8,7} implies RT^2_2 (Theorem 6.41). JRG^2_{2k,2n+1} implies DT^2_{k,n}, hence JRG^2_{8,7} implies ACA0 (Theorem 6.43). RG implies JRG over ACA0 (Corollary 6.29).

statement.name: (Strong) generalized Chubb–Hirst–McNicholl tree theorem
statement.definition: For f:[2^{<ω}]^n→k (all n-sets, not only chains) there is a perfect (resp. strong) subtree on which f uses at most ℓ colors.
statement.facts: (∀k)SCHMTT^n_{k,tsTT(n)} is provable in ACA0 and the bound is tight (Theorem 7.9). CHMTT^n_{k,tTT(n)} is provable in ACA0 and the bound is tight (Theorem 7.20).

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem for graphs, refined
statement.definition: Every infinite graph has an infinite H such that every vertex has 0, 1 or infinitely many neighbours in H, and every vertex of H has 0 or infinitely many neighbours in H.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.1.7), also for locally finite graphs; RCA0 proves it for highly recursive graphs; RSg ≡sW RSgr (cited from [27]).

statement.name: Weak Rival–Sands theorem for graphs (and refined)
statement.definition: Infinite H such that each x in H has ≤1 (resp. 0) or infinitely many neighbours in H.
statement.facts: Both equivalent to RT22 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.1.8); wRSg ≡c wRSgr; in computable degrees wRSg strictly below RT22 and lim, strictly above ADS and SRT22, incomparable with CAC; in Weihrauch degrees strictly below RT22, strictly above COH and RT1<∞ (both ≤sW wRSg), incomparable with lim, SRT22, SADC, DNR; SADC ≰W wRSgr, DNR ≰W wRSgr; SRT22 ≤W LPO ∗ wRSgr and SRT22 ≤W (LPO×LPO) ∗ wRSg; RT22 ≤W wRSg ∗ wRSg ∗ wRSg.

statement.name: Stable ascending/descending chain principle
statement.definition: Every infinite stable linear order has an infinite ascending or descending chain.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ SADS ↔ SADC; SADS ≡sc SADC; SADC <W SADS; SADC ≤sW SRT22; SADC ≰W wRSgr.

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem for posets with given chain decomposition / of width k
statement.definition: Every infinite poset with chain-decomposition-number k (resp. width k) has an infinite chain C such that every element is comparable with none or infinitely many elements of C.
statement.facts: RSpoCD_<∞ ↔ RSpoW_<∞ ↔ ADS + IΣ02; for standard k ≥ 3 both equivalent to ADS; RSpoCD_3 → ADS; over WKL0, RSpoW_2 ↔ SADS; RSpoW_2 strictly weaker than ADS, not computably true, has ω-models of low sets; open whether RSpoW_2 ↔ SADS over RCA0.

statement.name: Strong Rival–Sands theorems for posets
statement.definition: As RSpo but the chain is (0,cof)-homogeneous; sRSpoN for posets without infinite antichains.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ sRSpoCD_2 → ADS; ADS + IΣ02 ⊢ sRSpoCD_2; Π11-CA0 ⊢ sRSpoN; sRSpoN implies CAC and all RSpo principles.

statement.name: Maximal max-less chain principle
statement.definition: Every partial order has a ⊆-maximal chain among chains without maximum.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π11-CA0 over RCA0, also restricted to linear orders (Theorem 3.2.4).

statement.name: Chains in posets of bounded width / antichains in posets of bounded height
statement.definition: Every infinite poset of width k has an infinite chain; every infinite poset of height k has an infinite antichain.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves CC_k and CA_k for standard k; CC_<∞ and CA_<∞ are each equivalent to BΣ02 (Lemma 3.1.9).

statement.name: Bounded-oscillation stable Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: Every n-stable coloring of pairs (each x changes colour at most n times) has an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves n-SRT^2_k for standard n,k; n-SRT^2_N ↔ BΣ02.

statement.name: Bounded Ramsey theorem with fixed bound / higher exponents
statement.definition: Colorings of n-tuples with no 1-homogeneous set of size k have an infinite (0-)homogeneous set.
statement.facts: RCA0 + BΣ02 ⊢ bRT^2_k for standard k (computably true); bRT^{n+1}_{n+2} → RT^n_2; for n > 3 bRT^n_k ↔ ACA0; bRT^3_k admits cone avoidance; RT^n_k ≤sW bRT^{n+1}_{R(n,n+1,k)}.

statement.name: Unbalanced Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: Colorings of n-tuples with no infinite 1-homogeneous set; output an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: bRT^n ≤sW uRT^n; every uRT^2 instance has a solution computable in it; for n ≥ 3 every instance f has a solution computable in any degree PA over f^(n-2), hence Δ0n solutions.

statement.name: Specker–Larson principles (ω^2 is a partition ordinal)
statement.definition: Given a partition of N into infinitely many infinite sets and a coloring of pairs with no 1-homogeneous set of size k, there is an infinite 0-homogeneous set meeting infinitely many pieces infinitely (SSPL: every met piece infinitely).
statement.facts: SSPL_k → SPL_k → bRT^2_k; RCA0 + ∀k SPL_k ⊢ BΣ02; RCA0 + BΣ02 ⊢ SSPL_3 → SRT22; RT^4_64 → SSPL_3, so ACA0 ⊢ SSPL_3; SSPL_3 ≤W uRT^4, computable instances have Δ04 solutions.

statement.name: First-order part and unbounded star operator
statement.definition: First-order part of a problem; unbounded finite parallelization where the number of instances used is determined by convergence.
statement.facts: P* ≤W P^{u*} ≤W \hat P; for first-order Q, ^1(\hat Q) ≡W Q^{u*}; ^1 WKL ≡sW C_2^* (= K_N); ^1(WKL^(n)) ≡sW (C_2^*)^(n); ^1(\widehat{RT^n_k}) ≡W (C_2^*)^(n).

statement.name: Σ¹₁ unique choice, Σ¹₁ separation, Δ¹₁ comprehension and variants
statement.definition: Choice for Σ¹₁ singletons in Baire space; separation of sequences of pairs of trees (at most one ill-founded in each pair); comprehension variants.
statement.facts: All are strongly Weihrauch equivalent to UC_NN (Theorem 3.11).

statement.name: Arithmetical transfinite recursion as a function
statement.definition: Given Z, a well order X and an index of an arithmetical operator, output the hierarchy built along X.
statement.facts: ATR ≡sW UC_NN (Theorem 3.13).

statement.name: Π¹₁ separation, Σ¹₁ weak König's lemma, parallelized Σ¹₁ choice, diagonally non-hyperarithmetical functions
statement.definition: Higher analogues of Σ⁰₁ separation, WKL and DNC₂.
statement.facts: UC_NN <W \hat{Σ11-C2} ≡W Π11-Sep ≡W Σ11-WKL ≡W Π11-DNC2 <W \hat{Σ11-CN} ≤W C_NN (Theorem 4.3, Proposition 4.5). Σ11-WKL is closed under composition.

statement.name: Σ¹₁ weak weak König's lemma
statement.definition: Find a path through a Σ¹₁ binary tree of positive measure.
statement.facts: UC_NN <W UC_NN ⋆ Σ11-WWKL <W Σ11-WKL (Theorem 4.9). WKL ≰W Σ11-WWKL.

statement.name: Non-hyperarithmeticity problem
statement.definition: Given p, find q not hyperarithmetical relative to p.
statement.facts: NHA ≰W UC_NN and NHA ≤W C_NN.

statement.name: Comparability / weak comparability of well orderings
statement.definition: Given two well orders, find the strong comparison map (respectively some order-preserving map) between them.
statement.facts: CWO ≡sW UC_NN (Theorem 5.5). Whether WCWO ≡W UC_NN is left open (Question 5.8), later answered positively by Goh.

statement.name: One-sided perfect tree theorem and listing of countable closed sets
statement.definition: PTT1: find a perfect subtree of a tree with uncountably many paths. (w)List: enumerate a countable closed subset of Baire space.
statement.facts: PTT1 ≡W C_NN (Proposition 6.3); wList ≡W List ≡W UC_NN (Theorem 6.4).

statement.name: Listing finite / countable closed subsets of Cantor space; Π⁰₂ choice on N
statement.definition: Produce a tuple (resp. a list) of all elements of a finite (resp. countable nonempty) closed subset of Cantor space.
statement.facts: List_{2^N,<ω} ≡W Π02-CN. lim ≤W wList_{2^N,≤ω} ≤W UC_NN. For single-valued functions, being below wList_{2^N,≤ω} is the same as being below lim. The two list problems are Weihrauch incomparable. The threefold compositional power of wList_{2^N,≤ω} is ≡W UC_NN.

statement.name: Finding winning strategies / Nash equilibria in open and clopen games on Baire space
statement.definition: Find a winning strategy for the player known to win, or a pair of strategies one of which is winning.
statement.facts: FindWS_Π ≡W C_NN; FindWS_Δ ≡W Det_Δ ≡W FindWS_Σ ≡W UC_NN. C_NN <W Det_Σ. Det_Σ × C_NN ≰W Det_Σ. UC_NN × Det_Σ ≡W Det_Σ. TC_NN <W Det_Σ.

statement.name: Two-sided perfect tree theorem (weak/strong listing)
statement.definition: Output either a perfect subtree of T or a (weak or strong) listing of [T].
statement.facts: C_NN <W wPTT2 <W PTT2. LPO × wPTT2 ≰W wPTT2. NON × wPTT2 ≤W wPTT2. UC_NN × PTT2 ≡W PTT2. TC_NN <W wPTT2. Finite parallelizations: PTT2* ≡W Det_Σ* ≡W TC_NN*.

statement.notation: [if S_{Σ11} then C_NN else UC_NN], χ_{Π11}, TUC_NN
statement.name: If-then-else construction; characteristic function of a Π¹₁-complete set; total continuation of UC_NN
statement.definition: Combines C_NN and UC_NN according to a Σ¹₁ truth value.
statement.facts: PTT2 and Det_Σ are reducible to it, and it is strictly below TC_NN × C_NN. χ_{Π11} is not reducible to the parallelization of TC_NN (Corollary 8.6). A single-valued f is below the parallelization of TC_NN iff it is below UC_NN (Theorem 8.5).

statement.name: Growing grouping principle
statement.definition: For every c : [N]^2 → 2 there is a sequence of finite sets (G_i)_{i∈I} indexed by a cut, increasing, with c constant on G_i × G_j for i < j, |G_i| nondecreasing and unbounded.
statement.facts: WKL0* + ¬IΣ01 proves GGP22; RCA0* + ¬IΣ01 proves it for transitive colourings (Lemma 3.4). It is not arithmetically conservative over RCA0; RCA0 + GGP22 proves 2-DNC (Remark 3.5, Yokoyama).

statement.name: Σ02 separation principle
statement.definition: For any two disjoint Σ02 sets there is a Δ02 set separating them.
statement.facts: RCA0* ⊢ COH → Σ02-separation (Lemma 3.13). Σ02-separation fails in every model of the form (M, Δ1-Def(M)) (Lemma 3.14), hence COH is never 'computably true' over RCA0* (Theorem 3.15).

statement.name: Ramsey for transitive 2-colourings
statement.definition: RT22 restricted to transitive colourings.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ADS over RCA0* (Lemma 2.5). The analogous result for semitransitive colourings and CAC holds over RCA0* (Remark 2.6).

statement.name: Δ02 Ramsey theorem for pairs
statement.definition: Every Δ02(X) colouring of pairs has a Δ02(Y)-definable homogeneous set for some set Y.
statement.facts: RCA0 + BΣ02 + Δ02-RT22 is Π4- but not Π5-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ02 (Remark 2.26).

statement.name: Thin set theorem for all exponents
statement.definition: (∀n) TS^n: every coloring f:[N]^n→N has an infinite thin set.
statement.facts: Admits strong preservation of k hyperimmunities for every k (Corollary 8.4.2); RCA0 ∧ COH ∧ WKL ∧ TS^2_{k+1} ∧ TS does not imply STS^2_k over ω-models (Corollary 8.4.3).

statement.name: Thin set theorem for singletons with k colors
statement.definition: Every coloring f:N→k has an infinite set avoiding a color.
statement.facts: TS^1_{k+1} admits strong preservation of k hyperimmunities (Theorem 8.2.5); TS^1_k ≰sc TS^1_ℓ for ℓ>k≥2 (Corollary 8.2.6).

statement.name: Stable thin set theorem for pairs with k colors
statement.definition: TS^2_k restricted to stable colorings.
statement.facts: STS^2_k ≰c STS^2_ℓ for ℓ>k≥2 (Corollary 8.2.7); STS^2_k does not admit preservation of k hyperimmunities (Corollary 8.2.4); STS^n_k ≰c TS^n_{k+1} (Corollary 8.3.4); not implied by COH+WKL+TS^2_{k+1}+FS+TS.

statement.name: Stable diagonal non-computability
statement.definition: Every Δ02 function f has a function g with g(x)≠f(x) for all x.
statement.facts: Equivalent to SRRT^2_2 over RCA0+IΣ02 (Theorem 9.2.11); only Δ02 degree bounding it is 0' (Theorem 12.4.1).

statement.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem relativized to the jump
statement.definition: RRT^n_2 for ∅'-computable 2-bounded colorings.
statement.facts: wSRRT^{n+1}_2 ↔ RRT^n_2[0'] over RCA0+BΣ02 and computably equivalent (Theorem 9.3.1).

statement.name: Ramsey-type satisfiability for 2-branching clauses
statement.definition: RSAT restricted to sets of clauses where the i-th literal is a_i or ¬a_i.
statement.facts: Implies RWKL over RCA0 (Proposition 11.2.1); implied by RCOLOR3 (proof of Theorem 11.3.12).

statement.name: Thin-set version of a Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statement.definition: For every infinite tree T⊆k^{<ω} of colorings of [ω]^n, an infinite set thin for some path.
statement.facts: Π01(TS^1_2) is RWKL; admits c.b-enum avoidance under induction hypotheses (Theorem 13.5.9); RWKL admits simultaneous c.b-enum avoidance (Theorem 13.5.1).

statement.name: Free set / thin set theorems at other exponents
statement.definition: Free set theorem for colorings of n-tuples.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ RRT^{2n+1}_2 → FS^n (Theorem 9.0.11); FS admits strong preservation of k hyperimmunities (Theorem 8.5.1) and strong m c.b-enum avoidance (Corollary 13.6.2).

statement.name: Quantitative weak weak König's lemma
statement.definition: WWKL restricted to trees T with µ([T]) > ε; ≡sW P_{>ε}C_{2^N}.
statement.facts: ε-WWKL ≤W δ-WWKL iff ε ≥ δ (Theorem 10.1/Corollary 10.2). C_n ≰W 1/n-WWKL. WWKL ≤W ε-WWKL ∗ C_N, and WWKL^Δ ≡W ε-WWKL ∗ C_N for ε ∈ [0,1). Single-valued functions below (1/2-WWKL)^(n) are computable (Corollary 13.3). LPO ≤W ε-WWKL′ for ε < 1/2. 1/2-WWKL^Δ <W WWKL^Δ, and WWKL^Δ ≰W 1/2-WWKL^(n).

statement.name: Star version of quantitative WWKL
statement.definition: Input (n, T) with µ([T]) > 2^{-n}; output a path of T.
statement.facts: (1−∗)-WWKL <W ε-WWKL <W ∗-WWKL <W WWKL (Corollaries 10.6, 10.10). PCC_[0,1] ≰W ∗-WWKL and AUC_[0,1] ≰W ∗-WWKL.

statement.name: Lower counterpart of quantitative WWKL
statement.definition: Input a sequence (T_n) with µ([T_n]) > 1−2^{-n}; output a path of some T_n together with n.
statement.facts: (1−∗)-WWKL <W ε-WWKL for every ε ∈ (0,1).

statement.name: Positive connected choice on [0,1]
statement.definition: Closed choice on [0,1] restricted to proper intervals (connected closed sets of positive measure).
statement.facts: Join-irreducible. C_2^* ≤W PCC_[0,1] ≤W CN [10] and PCC_[0,1] ≤W WWKL. AUC_[0,1] <W PCC_[0,1]. PCC_[0,1] |W AUC_[0,1]^*. Not idempotent.

statement.name: All-or-unique choice on [0,1]
statement.definition: Closed choice on [0,1] restricted to the whole interval or singletons.
statement.facts: ≡sW RDIV. AUC_[0,1] <W PCC_[0,1] and hence <W WWKL. Not below ∗-WWKL, not sW below PC_[0,1]^(n). C_2 × AUC_[0,1] ≰W CC_[0,1] (so ≰W IVT). Not idempotent.

statement.name: Robust division
statement.definition: (x,y) ↦ x/max(x,y) if y ≠ 0, any point of [0,1] otherwise.
statement.facts: RDIV ≡sW AUC_[0,1]; RDIV <W WWKL (Corollary 16.4).

statement.name: Nash equilibria of bi-matrix games
statement.definition: Given a bi-matrix game, find a Nash equilibrium.
statement.facts: NASH is a cylinder; NASH ≡sW AUC_[0,1]^* (Pauly). NASH ≤W WWKL (Corollary 17.3), NASH ≰W IVT (Corollary 17.6), IVT |W NASH (Corollary 17.9).

statement.name: Lebesgue density lemma
statement.definition: Given a closed A ⊆ 2^N of positive measure and k, find w with µ(A ∩ w2^N)/2^{-|w|} ≥ 1 − 2^{-k}.
statement.facts: LDL ≡sW C_N (Theorem 11.2).

statement.name: Probabilistic choice on Baire space
statement.definition: Closed choice on N^N restricted to sets of positive measure (product geometric measure).
statement.facts: PC_N ≤sW PC_{N×2^N} ≤sW PC_{N^N}. Everything below PC_{N^N}^(n) is probabilistic, so WKL ≰W PC_{N^N}^(n). It is open whether WWKL′ ≤W PC_{N^N}.

statement.name: Probabilistic cluster point problem
statement.definition: Find a cluster point of a sequence whose set of cluster points has positive measure.
statement.facts: (P_I C_X)′ ≡sW P_I CL_X; WWKL′ ≡sW PCL_{2^N} ≡sW PCL_[0,1].

statement.name: Full open Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: Given an open set P ⊆ [N]^N, find a homogeneous solution (landing in or avoiding P).
statement.facts: Not ≤_W C_{N^N} (Cor. 4.15); wFindHSΠ01 <_W Σ01-RT (Cor. 4.16); TC_{N^N} ≤_W C_{2^N} ∗ Σ01-RT and χ_{Π11} <_W LPO ∗ Σ01-RT (Prop. 4.14); Σ01-RT ≰_W sTC_{N^N} × lim^{(n)} for all n (Thm. 4.20); Σ01-RT <_W NHA × Σ01-RT (Cor. 4.22); TC_{N^N} × C_{N^N} ≰_W f × Σ01-RT for hyperarithmetic f ≤_W C_{N^N} (Prop. 4.23); TC_{N^N} <_aW Σ01-RT (Cor. 5.13); Σ01-RT <_aW FindHSΣ01 (Thm. 5.14); (Σ01-RT)* ≡_aW TC_{N^N}*; id_2 not strongly Weihrauch reducible to it (Prop. 4.29); every computable instance has a solution <_T Kleene's O (Cor. 6.7).

statement.name: Strong open Ramsey theorem, open side
statement.definition: Given an open P with a homogeneous solution landing in P, find such a solution.
statement.facts: Closed under parallel product, a cylinder (Prop. 4.24, Cor. 4.25); sTC_{N^N} ≤_W FindHSΣ01, χ_{Π11} <_W FindHSΣ01 (Prop. 4.26); TC*_{N^N} <_W FindHSΣ01 (Cor. 4.27); C_{N^N} ∗ Σ01-RT ≤_W FindHSΣ01 (Thm. 4.28).

statement.name: Strong open Ramsey theorem, closed side
statement.definition: Given an open P with a homogeneous solution avoiding P, find such a solution.
statement.facts: C_{N^N} ≡_sW FindHSΔ01 ≡_sW FindHSΠ01 (Thm. 4.7).

statement.name: Weak open Ramsey theorem, open side
statement.definition: Restriction of FindHSΣ01 to open sets all of whose homogeneous solutions land in P.
statement.facts: UC_{N^N} ≡_W wFindHSΣ01 ≡_W wFindHSΔ01 (Thm. 4.5); not strongly above id_2 (Prop. 4.29); its total continuation is ≤_W ATR_2 (Prop. 4.13).

statement.name: Weak open Ramsey theorem, closed side
statement.definition: Restriction of FindHSΠ01 to open sets with no homogeneous solution landing in P.
statement.facts: UC_{N^N} <_W wFindHSΠ01 ≤_W C_{N^N} ≡_W C_{2^N} ∗ wFindHSΠ01 (Prop. 4.8, 4.9); closed under product (Prop. 4.10); \hat{Σ11-C^cof_N} ≤_sW wFindHSΠ01 (Thm. 4.11); not ≤_W ATR_2 (Cor. 4.12); ≡_aW C_{N^N} (Cor. 5.5).

statement.name: Full clopen Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: Given a clopen D ⊆ [N]^N, find a homogeneous solution.
statement.facts: UC_{N^N} ≡_W Δ01-RT (Thm. 4.6); not strongly above id_2.

statement.name: Strong clopen Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: Given a clopen D with a homogeneous solution landing in D, find such a solution.

statement.name: Weak clopen Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: Restriction of FindHSΔ01 to clopen D all of whose homogeneous solutions land in D.

statement.name: Strong total continuation of C_{N^N}
statement.definition: Given a tree, output a bit saying whether it is ill-founded and, if so, a path.
statement.facts: TC_{N^N} <_W sTC_{N^N}; \hat{TC_{N^N}} |_W sTC_{N^N} (Prop. 4.19); TC_{N^N} ≡_aW sTC_{N^N} (Thm. 5.8); f ≤_aW TC_{N^N} iff f ≤_W sTC_{N^N} × lim^{(n)} for some n (Thm. 5.12).

statement.name: Characteristic function of a Π¹₁-complete set
statement.definition: Given a tree on N, decide whether it is well-founded.
statement.facts: Not ≤_W C_{N^N}, not ≤_W TC*_{N^N} (cited from [18]).

statement.name: Non-hyperarithmeticity problem
statement.definition: Given p, find q not hyperarithmetic in p.
statement.facts: NHA ≤_W C_{N^N} (cited [18, Cor. 3.6]).

statement.name: Proper PAC learning problem
statement.definition: Given a closed concept class C ⊆ 2^N (full, positive or negative information) and d ≥ VCdim(C), find a learner A:S→C and a sample complexity m with which A properly PAC learns C; the <d versions drop d from the input and assume VCdim(C) < d.
statement.facts: PPAC ≡sW PPAC_{<d} ≡sW ERM ≡sW id (computable). PPAC_{<∞} ≡W C_N and ≡sW id × C_N ≡sW lim_Δ. PPAC^± ≡sW PPAC^±_{<d} ≡sW lim. PPAC^+_{<∞} ≡sW lim. PPAC^-_{<∞} ≡sW lim × C_N'.

statement.name: Improper PAC learning problem
statement.definition: As PPAC, but the learner may output arbitrary hypotheses in 2^N.
statement.facts: IPAC and IPAC^- are computable. IPAC_{<∞} ≡W C_N. IPAC^+ ≡sW WIT^+. DNC* ≤sW IPAC^+_{<2} ≤sW IPAC^+ <W WKL. PA <W IPAC^+_{<2}, and IPAC^+_{<2} ≰W WWKL^(n). IPAC^+ is not Las Vegas computable. WKL ≤sW C_N' ∗ IPAC^+. DNC* × C_N ≤W IPAC^+_{<∞} ≤W C_R.

statement.name: Relative PAC learning problem
statement.definition: Given C ∈ A^+, H ∈ A^- with C ⊆ H and d ≥ VCdim(C), find a learner into H with a sample complexity that PAC learns C relative to H.
statement.facts: RPAC ≡sW RPAC_{<d} ≡sW RPAC_fix ≡sW WKL. RPAC_{<∞} ≡sW C_R.

statement.name: VC dimension problems
statement.definition: Compute the VC dimension (in N∞) of a closed class, or an upper bound on it.
statement.facts: VCdim ≡sW VCdim^+ ≡sW SORT. VCdim^- ≡sW SORT'. VCdim_{<∞} ≡sW C_N. VCdim^-_{<∞} ≡sW C_N'. BVCdim ≡sW B.

statement.name: Witness problem
statement.definition: Given a closed class C and d ≥ VCdim(C), find a k-witness function for C.
statement.facts: WIT^- is computable. ACC_n ≰*_W WIT^+ for every n ≥ 2. DNC* ≤sW WIT^+ ≤sW WKL.

statement.name: Finitary DNC problem
statement.definition: Given instances of ACC_k^ for all k ≥ 2, find some k and a solution of the k-th instance.
statement.facts: PA <W DNC*. DNC_N <W DNC*. DNC* ≰W WWKL^(n) for every n.

statement.name: PA degree problem
statement.definition: Given p, find q of PA degree relative to p.
statement.facts: PA ≤sW DNC_k for every k. PA ≰W WWKL^(n) (cited). DNC_N ≰W PA (cited).

statement.name: Supremum, maximum, boundedness, discrete limit
statement.definition: Standard benchmark problems on sequences of natural numbers.
statement.facts: SORT ≡sW sup. SORT_{<∞} ≡sW max ≡sW C_N. B ≡W C_N ≡W lim_Δ ≡sW id × C_N. B <sW C_N <sW lim_Δ.

statement.name: Characteristic function of PAC learnability
statement.definition: Decide whether a closed concept class is PAC learnable.
statement.facts: χ_PL ≡sW χ_PL^+ ≡sW LPO'. χ_PL^- ≡sW LPO''.

statement.name: Bound for finite Π^1_1 sets
statement.definition: Given a finite Π^1_1 subset of N, return a bound for it (equivalent to Σ^1_1-C_N^cof).
statement.facts: Π11-Bound <_W DS; first-order part of DS is ≡_W Π11-Bound (Thm 4.10); Det_N(Π11-Bound) ≡_W C_N; RT^1_N <_W Π11-Bound; Π11-Bound not ≤_W C_N; UC_{N^N} <_W parallelization of Π11-Bound.

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle without bound given
statement.definition: Given a coloring c: N → k (k not given), find an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: RT^1_N <_W DS; a pointwise-finite problem is ≤_W DS iff it is ≤_W RT^1_N; problems with codomain k are ≤_W DS iff ≤_W RT^1_k.

statement.name: Descending/bad sequences in Γ-presented orders
statement.definition: DS/BS where the order is given by a Γ-name (Γ among Σ^0_k, Π^0_k, Δ^0_k, Σ^1_1, Π^1_1, Δ^1_1).
statement.facts: Γ^0_{k+1}-DS ≡_W Γ^0_1-DS ∗ lim^[k]; Δ^0_k-DS <_W Δ^0_{k+1}-DS; Π^0_k-DS ≡ Δ^0_{k+1}-DS ≡ Σ^0_{k+1}-DS; Σ^0_k-DS ≡ Δ^0_k-DS; Det(Δ^0_k-DS) ≡ lim^[k]; LPO^(k) ≤_W Σ^0_k-BS, so Σ^0_k-BS ≰_W Σ^0_k-DS; Δ^1_1-DS ≡ DS ∗ UC_{N^N}; Δ^1_1-DS <_W Σ^1_1-DS <_W C_{N^N}; ATR_2 |_W Σ^1_1-DS; Π^1_1-CA ≤_W Σ^1_1-BS and Π^1_1-CA ≤_W Π^1_1-DS; Σ^1_1-DS <_W Σ^1_1-BS.

statement.name: General stable ascending/descending sequence
statement.definition: Given a linear order of type ω+n, n+ω* or ω+ω*, produce an infinite ascending or descending sequence.
statement.facts: LPO′ ≤_W FindS^{ω,n+ω*} (a restriction of General-SADS); General-SADS |_W DS.

statement.name: Finding suborders/sequences in linear orders
statement.definition: FindC: find a suborder of a type in Y; FindS: find an ascending or descending sequence with indication of direction.
statement.facts: LPO′ ≤_W FindS^{ω,n+ω*}; FindS^{ω,n+ω*} |_W DS; FindC^{ω,n+ω*} ≤_W DS.

statement.name: Π^1_1 comprehension as a problem
statement.definition: Given a sequence of trees, decide which are well-founded (parallelization of χ_{Π^1_1}).

statement.name: Σ^1_1 choice on N
statement.definition: Choose an element of a nonempty Σ^1_1 subset of N.
statement.facts: First-order part of C_{N^N} ≡_W Σ^1_1-C_N ≡_W first-order part of Σ^1_1-DS; parallelization of Σ^1_1-C_N ≤_W Σ^1_1-DS.

statement.name: Two-sided ATR
statement.definition: Given (L, A), produce either a descending sequence through L or a jump hierarchy on L from A.

statement.name: Weak limited principle of omniscience
statement.definition: For every binary sequence (a_n), either all a_n = 0 or it is not the case that all a_n = 0.
statement.facts: Over intuitionistic logic (with countable choice) it is equivalent to the existence of a discontinuous function from 2^N to {0,1}, from N^N to N, or from [0,1] to R, to the existence of a bijection [0,1) -> (0,1), and to a version of the Rising Sun Lemma. It lies strictly between LPO and LLPO, and WLPO <-> WPFP + MP_or.

statement.name: Markov's principle
statement.definition: Every almost positive real number is positive; equivalently, for a binary sequence that is not identically 0 there is n with a_n = 1.
statement.facts: LPO <-> WLPO + MP and MP <-> MP_or + WMP. It holds in RUSS and in CLASS.

statement.name: Weak Markov's principle
statement.definition: Every pseudo-positive real number is positive.
statement.facts: Equivalent to every real-valued function on 2^N (or on [0,1], N^N, N_inf, or a two-point space) being strongly extensional. Under WMP, LPO and WLPO are equivalent. It fails in the topological model X_U.

statement.name: Disjunctive Markov's principle
statement.definition: Every almost positive real number is pseudo-positive; equivalently, the De Morgan law for Pi^0_1 formulas.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL!!! (a unique-path variant of WKL) and to a uniqueness-restricted intermediate value theorem. It is implied by LLPO.

statement.name: Fan theorems for decidable, c-, Pi^0_1-, stable and arbitrary bars
statement.definition: Every bar of the given complexity in 2^* is uniform.
statement.facts: FAN_Delta is equivalent to POS (every positive uniformly continuous function on [0,1] has a positive infimum) and to Dini's theorem. FAN_c is equivalent to the anti-Specker property AS_[0,1] and to uniform continuity of pointwise continuous f: 2^N -> N. They are linked by FAN_full => FAN_stable => FAN_Pi01 => UCT => FAN_c => FAN_Delta. Over intuitionistic logic, WKL (equivalently LLPO) implies UCT.

statement.name: Uniform continuity theorem
statement.definition: Every pointwise continuous f: [0,1] -> R is uniformly continuous.
statement.facts: Equivalent to every pointwise continuous function on [0,1] or 2^N being bounded, to separability of C([0,1]), and to FAN_c + MC.

statement.name: Boundedness principle for countable sets
statement.definition: Every inhabited, countable, pseudobounded subset of N is bounded.
statement.facts: Equivalent to every sequentially continuous map N^N -> N being pointwise continuous (or locally bounded). It implies FAN_c -> FAN_Pi01.

statement.name: Kleene tree, Specker sequence, singular cover existence
statement.definition: Recursive counterexample principles: KT is the existence of an infinite decidable binary tree without paths, SS the existence of a sequence in [0,1] eventually bounded away from every point, SC the existence of a singular cover.
statement.facts: The hierarchy is SC => KT => SS. KT is equivalent to the failure of POS-type statements, and SS to the existence of an unbounded pointwise continuous function on [0,1].

statement.name: n-ary lesser limited principle of omniscience
statement.definition: For a binary sequence with at most one 1 and a partition of N into n parts, some part contains only zeros.
statement.facts: Equivalent to its arithmetic-progression version and to a statement about products of reals. It fails in topological models over metric spaces with an accumulation point.

statement.name: Lindenbaum's Lemma
statement.definition: Every consistent set of sentences can be extended to a complete consistent theory.
statement.facts: Computably equivalent to WKL; equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Simpson). The version for consistent theories is provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Paris-Harrington principle
statement.definition: For each n, k, l there is u such that every k-coloring of [X]^n with |X| ≥ u has a homogeneous set H with |H| ≥ l and min H ≥ |H|.
statement.facts: RCA0 + RT ⊢ PH; not provable in PA, so not in ACA0; hence RT strictly stronger than ACA0.

statement.name: Well-founded partial orders have well-ordered linear extensions
statement.definition: Every well-founded partial order has a well-ordered linear extension.
statement.facts: Implies WKL0 over RCA0; provable in ACA0; computably well-founded computable partial order with no computably well-founded computable linear extension; open whether it implies ACA0.

statement.name: Weak extendibility of order types
statement.definition: Every countable partial order avoiding τ has a linear extension avoiding τ.
statement.facts: EXT(ζ) equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0; EXT(η) provable in Π11-CA0 and in ATR0 + IΣ11; Miller: EXT(η) implies WKL0 over a stronger base.

statement.name: Dushnik-Miller theorem
statement.definition: Every infinite (countable) linear order has a nontrivial self-embedding.
statement.facts: Not computably true; equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0; every computable infinite linear order has a ∅″-computable nontrivial self-embedding, but not necessarily a ∅′-computable one.

statement.name: Jullien's theorem
statement.definition: Characterization of the weakly extendible countable order types.
statement.facts: RCA0 + JUL ⊢ FRA; RCA0 + IΣ11 + FRA ⊢ JUL (Montalbán).

statement.name: Kruskal's theorem
statement.definition: Finite trees are wqo under embeddability.
statement.facts: Not provable in ATR0 (Friedman); exact strength by Rathjen and Weiermann.

statement.name: Π01 genericity variant
statement.definition: Principle of Hirschfeldt, Lange, Shore related to Π01G.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 + IΣ02, not in RCA0, implies no new first-order statements.

statement.name: Atomic trees are strongly atomic
statement.definition: Every atomic binary tree with no dead ends is strongly atomic.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BΣ02 over RCA0.

statement.name: König's lemma for bounded trees with given bound
statement.definition: Every infinite tree bounded by a given function f has a path.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Atomic/prime model statements
statement.definition: Every atomic structure is prime; every complete atomic theory has a prime model; any two atomic models of a complete theory are isomorphic.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Peano arithmetic degree problem
statement.definition: PA : D ⇒ D, b ↦ {a : a ≫ b} (degrees of PA over b).
statement.facts: NON ≤sW PA; PA ≰W NON; ACC_N ≰W PA; PA ≡sW [DNC_n] for all n ≥ 2 (hence PA ≡sW [WKL]); PA ≤sW J_D and J_D ≰W PA; PA is not probabilistic; PA ≰W WWKL^(k) for all k; PA′ ≡sW PA ∘ J_D.

statement.name: Weak 1-genericity problem
statement.definition: Given q, find p weakly 1-generic relative to q.
statement.facts: HYP ≤sW 1-WGEN and 1-WGEN ≤W HYP, so HYP ≡W 1-WGEN (strong equivalence open, Question 9.6); 1-WGEN ≤W COH.

statement.name: Low Basis Theorem problem
statement.definition: Given an infinite binary tree T, find a path p with p′ ≤T T′.
statement.facts: WKL <W LBT <W L; LPO ≰W LBT; LBT |W C_R; LBT is discriminative.

statement.name: Kleene–Post theorem problem
statement.definition: Given r, find ⟨p,q⟩ with r ≤T ⟨p,q⟩ and p |T q.
statement.facts: KPT ≤sW MLR and KPT ≤sW 1-GEN, both strict.

statement.name: Friedberg jump inversion theorem; inverse of the Turing jump on degrees
statement.definition: JIT : D ⇒ D, a ↦ {b : b′ = a ∪ 0′}; J_D^{-1} is its restriction to the cone above 0′.
statement.facts: J_D^{-1} <sW JIT <sW c_∅′ × id; JIT ≤sW lim_J (strict); J_D^{-1} is not computable; JIT is continuous and limit computable but not computable; J_D^{-1} ∗s J_D^{-1} ≡sW 0; JIT ∗ JIT ≤W c_∅′ ≤W lim.

statement.name: Diagonally non-computable functions with k values; WKL for big k-branching trees; all-or-co-unique choice on n
statement.definition: DNC_X(p) = {q ∈ X^N : q(n) ≠ φ^p_n(n) for all n}; WKL_k finds paths in big trees in k*; ACC_n is choice on n with at most one element missing.
statement.facts: DNC_k ≡sW WKL_k ≡sW \hat{ACC_k}; ACC_n ≰W DNC_{n+1}; DNC_N <W DNC_{n+1} <W DNC_n; DNC_n is indiscriminative for n ≥ 3; DNC_2 ≤W C_N′ ∗ DNC_k; DNC_n is not probabilistic; MLR |W DNC_3; WKL_n |W (k−1)/k-WWKL for n ≥ 3, k ≥ 2.

statement.name: Quantitative weak weak König's lemma variants
statement.definition: ε-WWKL finds a path in a tree of measure > ε; (1−∗)-WWKL: given (T_n) with µ[T_n] > 1 − 2^{−n}, find a path in some T_n.
statement.facts: MLR <sW (1−∗)-WWKL; ACC_N <sW (1−∗)-WWKL; (1−∗)-WWKL is strongly parallelizable; DNC_N <sW (1−∗)-WWKL; ACC_{n+1} ≤sW (n−1)/n-WWKL and ACC_n ≰W (n−1)/n-WWKL; ε-WWKL is not parallelizable for ε ∈ [0,1).

statement.notation: lim_J, L, L_2, J_D, c_∅′ × id
statement.name: Restricted limit, low map, low2 map, Turing jump on degrees, constant halting problem
statement.definition: lim_J is lim restricted to sequences whose jumps converge; L = J^{-1}∘lim; L_2 = J^{-1}∘J^{-1}∘lim∘lim; J_D(a) = a′.
statement.facts: DNC_N ≰W lim_J; MLR ≰W lim_J; C_N ≤W lim_J; LBT ≤sW L; COH ≤sW L_2 and COH ≰sW L; WBWT_R ≤sW L_2 and WBWT_R ≰sW L; lim ∗s lim^{-1} ≡sW c_∅′ × id.

statement.name: Cohesiveness for enumerated sequences
statement.definition: COH with the sets R_i given by positive information (enumerations).
statement.facts: COH ≤sW COH+ ≤sW COH′; COH+ ≰W COH; 1-GEN ≰W COH+; ACC_N ≰W COH+; COH+ ≤sW lim′.

statement.name: Degree versions of problems
statement.facts: [COH] ≡sW J_D^{-1} ∘ PA ∘ J_D; [COH] ≤sW PA′; [COH] ≡W (lim → PA′) ≡W (JD → PA′) ≡W (lim → [WKL]′).

statement.name: Weak and subsequential Bolzano–Weierstraß theorems
statement.definition: WBWT_X outputs a sequence converging to a name of a cluster point; SBWT_X outputs a strictly monotone s with (x_{s(n)}) convergent.
statement.facts: WBWT_R is densely realized (ω-indiscriminative); WBWT_X ≡W (lim → BWT_X); WBWT_X ≡W SBWT_X; SBWT_{2^N} ≡sW SBWT_R ≡sW SBWT_[0,1] ≡sW SBWT_{[0,1]^N}; SBWT_R ≡sW COH; COH ≡W \hat{WBWT_2}; BWT_R ≡W lim ∗ WBWT_R; WBWT_R is low2 but not low.

statement.name: Weihrauch implication (residual)
statement.definition: f → g = min{h : g ≤W f ∗ h}.
statement.facts: COH ≡W (lim → WKL′) (Corollary 14.9); WBWT_X ≡W (lim → BWT_X).

statement.name: Infinitary pigeonhole principle (color-finding version)
statement.definition: Instances: f: ω→ω with bounded range; solutions: all i such that f^{-1}{i} is infinite.
statement.facts: Does not uniformly admit computable solutions (Prop 3.7.2). RT^1 ≡W IPHP ≡W General-IPHP (Prop 4.3.4); computably equivalent to RT^1 and FUF (Prop 4.2.10). IPHP ≰W IPHP+ (Prop 4.3.6). RT^1_2 ≰sW IPHP and IPHP ≰sW RT^1 (Prop 4.4.4). TJ is uniformly identity reducible to its parallelization (Prop 4.1.4), whose converse fails even under ≤c (Prop 4.2.11), but the parallelization is computably reducible to two applications of TJ (Prop 4.5.3).

statement.name: IPHP with number of colors given
statement.definition: Instances: pairs (k,f) with f: ω→k; solutions: i with f^{-1}{i} infinite.
statement.facts: IPHP+ ≡c IPHP, IPHP+ is uniformly identity reducible to IPHP, and IPHP ≰W IPHP+.

statement.name: Infinitary pigeonhole principle over general sets
statement.definition: Instances: families {X_i} of subsets of ω with infinite union and almost all X_i empty; solutions: i with X_i infinite.
statement.facts: ≡W RT^1 and IPHP (Prop 4.3.4); General-IPHP ≡sW IPHP (Prop 4.4.3).

statement.name: Finite unions principle
statement.definition: Instances: families of finite sets F_i, almost all empty; solutions: numbers bounding the union.
statement.facts: Computably equivalent to RT^1 (Prop 4.2.10); FUF ≤W RT^1 but RT^1_2 ≰W FUF (Prop 4.3.5).

statement.name: Weak König's lemma, disjunctive form
statement.definition: Instances: all trees T ⊆ 2^{<ω}; solutions: paths if T is infinite, otherwise lengths ℓ at which T has no string.
statement.facts: WKL is a subproblem of Disj-WKL; Disj-WKL is identity reducible to WKL but not uniformly so (Prop 4.1.5).

statement.name: Heine–Borel theorem for [0,1] (and its disjunctive form)
statement.definition: HBT: given open intervals covering [0,1], find ℓ such that the first ℓ intervals cover. Disj-HBT: given any sequence of intervals, find such an ℓ or an uncovered point.
statement.facts: Disj-HBT admits solutions in PA (Prop 3.8.1) and codes PA (Prop 3.8.3); Disj-HBT ≡c WKL (Cor 4.2.6). HBT admits computable solutions.

statement.name: Brouwer's fan theorem
statement.definition: Instances: bars B ⊆ 2^{<ω}; solutions: finite subsets of B that are bars.
statement.facts: FAN ≤W WKL but WKL ≰c FAN; FAN admits computable solutions (Prop 4.3.8).

statement.name: Finitary Ramsey's theorem
statement.definition: For n,k,m there is N such that every k-coloring of [X]^n with |X| ≥ N has a homogeneous set of size m; problem forms: bounding or finding Ramsey numbers.
statement.facts: None.

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem (subsequence version)
statement.definition: Instances: bounded sequences of reals; solutions: convergent subsequences (unlike the catalogue's cluster-point version).
statement.facts: None.

statement.name: Sequential compactness of Cantor space
statement.definition: Instances: sequences R_i of elements of 2^ω; solutions: infinite S such that for each e, R_i(e) is constant for almost all i ∈ S. It is COH with instances transposed.
statement.facts: Admits PA avoidance (Prop 3.8.5), omits PA solutions (Prop 3.8.6), and is uniformly identity equivalent to COH (Prop 4.1.7).

statement.name: k-valued DNC problem
statement.definition: Instances: sets X; solutions: k-valued functions DNC relative to X.
statement.facts: WKL ≡W DNR_2; DNR_j ≡c DNR_k; DNR_k ≤W DNR_j for j<k; DNR_j ≰W DNR_k for k>j (Theorem 4.3.11, Jockusch).

statement.name: Existence of linear extensions
statement.definition: Instances: partial orders on ω; solutions: their linear extensions.
statement.facts: Uniformly identity reducible to WKL.

statement.name: Church's thesis as a problem
statement.definition: Instances: total functions f; solutions: indices e with f = Φ_e.
statement.facts: Computably true but does not admit computable solutions.

statement.name: Δ¹₁ comprehension
statement.definition: RCA0 plus comprehension for sets defined by a Σ¹₁ formula whose complement is also Σ¹₁.
statement.facts: Δ¹₁-CA0 ⊢ ACA0+ (Prop 5.8.15(1)). There is an ω-model of ACA0+ + ¬Δ¹₁-CA0 (Prop 5.8.15(2)). ATR0 ⊢ Δ¹₁-CA0 (Prop 5.8.21(1)). HYP is an ω-model of Δ¹₁-CA0 + ¬ATR0 (Prop 5.8.21(2)), and HYP is the minimum ω-model of Δ¹₁-CA0.

statement.name: Σ¹₁ separation principle
statement.definition: For Σ¹₁ formulas φ, ψ defining disjoint classes, there is a set Z containing the first and disjoint from the second.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5.8.20, Simpson). Implies ACA0 over RCA0. Π¹₁ separation is equivalent to it over RCA0.

statement.name: Existence of ranges of functions
statement.definition: The range of every function N → N exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5.7.2).

statement.name: Existence of hyperjumps
statement.definition: For every X, the hyperjump of X exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5.8.6).

statement.name: Set of indices of ill-founded trees
statement.definition: For every sequence of subtrees T_i of N^<N, the set of i such that T_i has an infinite path exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5.8.9, proof left as Exercise 5.13.22).

statement.name: König's lemma for trees with at most two immediate successors per node
statement.definition: KL restricted to subtrees of N^<N in which each node has at most two immediate successors.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 and to KL over RCA0 (Theorem 5.7.3).

statement.name: Leftmost path principle for binary trees
statement.definition: Every infinite tree on {0,1} has a leftmost path.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Exercise 5.13.23(1)).

statement.name: Extraction of a homogeneous set from a limit homogeneous set
statement.definition: For every c : [N]^2 → 2 with lim_y c(x,y) = 1 for all x, there is an infinite set H with c(x,y) = 1 for all pairs of H.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RT1 (hence to BΣ02) over RCA0 (Proposition 6.5.3, Dzhafarov–Hirschfeldt–Reitzes). Uniformly computably true.

statement.name: Stable ascending/descending chain principle
statement.definition: Every infinite stable linear order has an infinite ascending chain (all elements small in it) or descending chain (all elements large in it).
statement.facts: SADC ≡_c SADS. In Figure 9.2 it lies below SADS under (strong) Weihrauch reducibility.

statement.name: Chain/antichain principle for ω-ordered partial orders
statement.definition: Every infinite ω-ordered partial order (x ≤_P y implies x ≤ y) has an infinite chain or antichain.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ CAC ↔ CAC^ord (Prop. 9.2.31). CAC^ord admits Δ^0_2 solutions, hence CAC ≰_c CAC^ord (Thm. 9.2.32).

statement.name: Stable chain/antichain principle for ω-ordered partial orders
statement.definition: Every infinite ω-ordered stable partial order has an infinite ω-ordered chain or antichain.
statement.facts: SCAC ≡_c SCAC^ord (Thm. 9.2.33). SCAC ≰_W SCAC^ord and SCAC ≰_sc SCAC^ord (Thm. 9.2.34).

statement.notation: RT22 restricted to semi-transitive / transitive colorings
statement.name: Semi-transitive and transitive Ramsey's theorem for pairs
statement.definition: RT^2_2 restricted to colorings in which all but at most one color (resp. every color) is transitive.
statement.facts: Over RCA0 (via identity reductions), the semi-transitive version is equivalent to CAC and the transitive version to ADS. The stable versions are equivalent to SCAC and SADS (Prop. 9.2.12).

statement.name: Product form of Milliken's tree theorem
statement.definition: For d ≥ 1 and rooted, meet-closed, finitely branching trees T_0..T_{d-1} of height ω without leaves, every k-coloring of S_n(T_0,…,T_{d-1}) is constant on S_n(S_0,…,S_{d-1}) for some tuple of strong subtrees of height ω sharing a level function. PMTT^1 is the Halpern–Läuchli theorem.
statement.facts: PMTT^1 admits computable solutions (Thm 9.7.6). ACA0 proves PMTT^n_k. For n ≥ 3, PMTT^n is equivalent to ACA. PMTT is equivalent to ACA0' over RCA0 and PMTT ≡W MTT. PMTT^2 admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Thm 9.7.8).

statement.name: Finite unions theorem
statement.definition: Every finite coloring of P_fin(ω) has an infinite family U with the apartness property such that the coloring is constant on the finite unions FU(U).
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ HT ↔ FUT and HT ≡W FUT (Prop 9.9.14).

statement.notation: HT with apartness; HT^{=n}_k / HT^{≤n}_k with apartness
statement.name: Hindman's theorem (and bounded-sum versions) with apartness
statement.definition: The corresponding Hindman-type statement where the solution must also satisfy the apartness property (μ(x) < λ(y) for x < y).
statement.facts: HT is equivalent to HT with apartness over RCA0 and Weihrauch (Thm 9.9.9). RCA0 ⊢ HT^{≤n}_{2k} → HT^{≤n}_k with apartness, and the latter ≤sc HT^{≤n}_{2k} (Thm 9.9.31). For n ≥ 3, k ≥ 2, HT^{=n}_k with apartness ↔ ACA0 (Thm 9.9.32). HT^{≤2}_2 with apartness → ACA0, hence HT^{≤2}_4 → ACA0 (Thm 9.9.33). HT^{=2}_2 with apartness → IPT^2_2 (Thm 9.9.36).

statement.name: n intersection principle
statement.definition: Every nontrivial family of sets has a maximal subfamily satisfying the n-intersection property (any n members have nonempty intersection).
statement.facts: FIP → mIP → nIP for m > n ≥ 2 over RCA0. nIP ≡c FIP ≡c 1-GEN, and RCA0 + IΣ2 ⊢ nIP ↔ 1-GEN (Thm 9.10.23).

statement.name: Weak weak König's lemma with measure bound q
statement.definition: For rational 0 < q < 1: every tree T ⊆ 2^{<ω} with lim |T ∩ 2^n|/2^n ≥ q has a path.
statement.facts: p-WWKL ≡sc q-WWKL and RCA0 ⊢ q-WWKL ↔ WWKL (Thm 9.11.12). For p < q, p-WWKL ≰W q-WWKL (Prop 9.11.13).

statement.name: Weak comparability of well orderings
statement.definition: For all X, Y with WO(X) and WO(Y), either X embeds into Y or Y embeds into X.
statement.facts: RCA0 + WCWO proves ACA0 (Proposition 12.1.11, Friedman). RCA0 + WCWO proves the Σ11 axiom of choice (Proposition 12.1.12). Over RCA0, WCWO is equivalent to ATR0 and to SCWO (Theorem 12.1.13, Friedman; see Hirst and Friedman).

statement.name: Strong comparability of well orderings
statement.definition: For all X, Y with WO(X) and WO(Y), either X strongly embeds into Y (onto an initial segment) or Y strongly embeds into X.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, SCWO is equivalent to ATR0 and to WCWO (Theorem 12.1.13).

statement.name: Open determinacy for Gale–Stewart games
statement.definition: Every Gale–Stewart game G(S) on ω with open winning class S is determined.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to ATR0 and to clopen determinacy (Theorem 12.3.4, Steel).

statement.name: Clopen determinacy for Gale–Stewart games
statement.definition: Every Gale–Stewart game G(S) with clopen winning class S is determined.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to ATR0 and to open determinacy (Theorem 12.3.4); the proof shows clopen determinacy implies ACA0 over RCA0. Determinacy for intersections of open and closed classes is equivalent to Π11-CA0 (Tanaka, cited).

statement.name: Higher levels of Borel determinacy
statement.definition: Determinacy of Gale–Stewart games whose winning class is Σ^0_4 (resp. a finite difference hierarchy level n-Π^0_3 of Π^0_3 classes).
statement.facts: Z2 does not prove Σ^0_4 determinacy (Theorem 12.3.14, Friedman; Martin). Π^1_{n+2}-CA0 proves n-Π^0_3 determinacy, while Δ^1_{n+2}-CA0 with full induction does not (Theorem 12.3.3, Montalbán–Shore, cited).

statement.notation: Existence of evaluation maps for (trivial) Borel codes
statement.name: Evaluation maps for Borel codes
statement.definition: For every (trivial) Borel code B and every X there is an evaluation map for B at X; equivalently for every Borel code B and X, X ∈ B or X ∉ B.
statement.facts: Each version is equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 12.2.4, Dzhafarov–Flood–Solomon–Westrick; Corollary 12.2.5). Uniqueness of evaluation maps is provable in ACA0.

statement.name: Lusin separation for analytic codes
statement.definition: If analytic codes A0, A1 have no common point, there is a Borel code B containing the points of A0 and excluding the points of A1.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 12.2.9, Simpson, cited).

statement.name: Nested interval choice (Brattka–Gherardi)
statement.definition: Instance: a nested sequence of rational intervals [a_n,b_n] ⊆ [0,1] with a_n ≤ a_{n+1} ≤ b_{n+1} ≤ b_n. Solution: a real x with a_n ≤ x ≤ b_n for all n.
statement.facts: IVT ≡sW B (Theorem 10.4.3). Cited from Brattka–Gherardi: B is equivalent to C_I, choice for closed intervals.

statement.name: Iterated Hindman's theorem
statement.definition: For every sequence of 2-colorings ⟨C_i⟩ there is an increasing sequence ⟨x_i⟩ such that for each j, {x_i : i > j} satisfies Hindman's theorem for C_j.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to IHT_{<ω}, AUF and MT^n for n ≥ 3. Provable in ACA0+ (Blass–Hirst–Simpson). Equivalent over ACA0 to the Auslander–Ellis theorem (Theorem 10.6.15, Corollary 10.6.16). Open whether HT implies IHT (Question 10.6.18).

statement.name: Almost downward translation invariant ultrafilters
statement.definition: Every countable downward translation algebra has an almost downward translation invariant ultrafilter.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IHT over RCA0, and to the Auslander–Ellis theorem over ACA0.

statement.name: Milliken–Taylor theorem for exponent n
statement.definition: If f : [N]^n → k then there is an increasing sequence X such that f is constant on FS^n(X).
statement.facts: For each n ≥ 3, equivalent to IHT over RCA0, and to the Auslander–Ellis theorem over ACA0.

statement.name: Birkhoff recurrence for Cantor space systems
statement.definition: Every compact dynamical system over Cantor space has a recurrent point.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Day).

statement.name: Vector space basis for n-dimensional spaces
statement.definition: Instance: an n-dimensional vector space over Q (n ≥ 2). Solution: a basis.
statement.facts: VSB_n ≡W C_N for all n ≥ 2 (Hirst–Mummert, Theorem 11.2.5).

statement.name: Every vector space has a basis
statement.definition: Every vector space over a field K (or over Q) has a basis.
statement.facts: Equivalent to TJ under ≤c and to ACA0 over RCA0. The version for spaces of bounded dimension is equivalent to IΣ02 (Theorem 11.2.3).

statement.name: Every commutative ring has a prime ideal
statement.definition: Every commutative ring has a prime ideal.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL under ≤c and over RCA0.

statement.name: Every commutative ring has a maximal ideal
statement.definition: Every commutative ring has a maximal ideal.
statement.facts: Equivalent to TJ under ≤c and to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Orderability of fields and groups
statement.definition: Every formally real field is orderable; every torsion-free abelian group is orderable; every torsion-free nilpotent group is orderable.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to WKL under ≤c and over RCA0.

statement.name: Induced ordering on quotients by convex normal subgroups
statement.definition: If G is an orderable group and N a convex normal subgroup of G, the induced ordering on G/N exists.
statement.facts: For linearly orderable G it is computably true and provable in RCA0. For partially orderable G it is equivalent to TJ under ≤c and to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Nielsen–Schreier theorem for presented subgroups
statement.definition: For every X and every S ⊆ F_X, the subgroup ⟨S⟩ presented by S is free.
statement.facts: Equivalent to TJ under ≤c and to ACA0 over RCA0. The version for subgroups given as sets is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 11.5.5).

statement.name: Noetherian rings have finitely many prime ideals
statement.definition: Every Noetherian ring has only finitely many prime ideals.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ WKL + CAC → NFP → TAC (Conidis's TAC). WKL0 does not prove NFP, and NFP does not imply ACA0 over ω-models. Open whether NFP → WKL.

statement.name: Every Artinian ring is Noetherian
statement.definition: Every Artinian ring is Noetherian (with related variants on local Artinian rings and the Jacobson radical).
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Conidis).

statement.name: Π⁰₁ separation
statement.definition: For disjoint Π01-definable sets there is a set separating them.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Bounded Σ⁰₁ comprehension
statement.definition: ∀n ∃X ∀i (i ∈ X ↔ (i < n ∧ φ(i))) for Σ⁰₁ formulas φ.
statement.facts: It is provable in RCA0 (Theorem II.3.9). Over the basic axioms, induction axiom and Δ⁰₁ comprehension it is equivalent to Σ⁰₁ induction (Remark II.3.11).

statement.notation: Baire category theorem; Banach–Steinhaus; Tietze (closed set version)
statement.name: RCA0-provable theorems of analysis
statement.definition: Nested interval completeness, uncountability of R, Baire category theorem for complete separable metric spaces, paracompactness, Tietze extension for closed sets, Banach–Steinhaus.
statement.facts: All are provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Transfinite induction schemes
statement.definition: ACA0 plus transfinite induction along every countable well ordering for Π¹ₖ (resp. Σ¹ₖ) formulas; Π¹∞-TI0 is the union over k.
statement.facts: Every β-model satisfies Π¹∞-TI0 (Lemma VII.2.15). Π¹₁-CA0 proves the existence of a countable coded β-model of Π¹∞-TI0 (Theorem VII.2.16). ATR0 is provable from Π¹∞-TI0 (Corollary VII.2.19). Π¹∞-TI0 is not finitely axiomatizable (Corollary VII.2.23). For AΠ¹₁ sentences, provability in Π¹∞-TI0 is equivalent to provability in ACA0 plus the existence of HJ(∅) (Corollary VII.2.21). Σ¹₁-TI0 is equivalent to ATR0 plus Σ¹₁-IND (Remark VII.2.20).

statement.name: Existence of hyperjumps and of countable coded β-models
statement.definition: The hyperjump HJ(X) is the complete Σ¹₁(X) set. A countable coded β-model is a coded ω-model that is correct for Σ¹₁ formulas.
statement.facts: An ω-model of RCA0 is a β-model of Π¹₁-CA0 iff it is closed under hyperjump (Theorem VII.1.8). Π¹₁-CA0 is equivalent over ACA0 to 'every X belongs to some countable coded β-model' (Theorem VII.2.10). Π¹₁-CA0 is equivalent over RCA0 to the totality of the hyperjump (Exercise VII.1.16). ACA0 proves that every countable coded β-model satisfies ATR0 (Theorem VII.2.7). ATR0 does not prove the existence of a countable coded β-model (Corollary VII.2.8).

statement.name: Strong comprehension schemes
statement.definition: ACA0 plus comprehension for Π¹ₖ formulas, resp. for Δ¹ₖ-definable sets; Π¹∞-CA0 is the union over k.
statement.facts: ∆¹ₖ-CA0 ⊆ Π¹ₖ-CA0 ⊆ ∆¹ₖ₊₁-CA0, with all inclusions proper (Remarks VII.5.2). Each of these theories has a minimum β-model of the form Lα(X), and these models are distinct (Theorem VII.5.17, Corollary VII.7.10). Adding ∃X∀Y(Y ∈ L(X)) is conservative for Π¹₄ sentences (Corollary VII.5.11). Π¹ₖ₊₁-CA0 proves the existence of a countable coded β-model of ∆¹ₖ₊₁-CA0 (Corollary VII.7.9). ∆¹₂-CA0 fails in the minimum β-model of Π¹₁-CA0 (Exercise VII.5.7).

statement.name: Choice, dependent choice and induction schemes
statement.definition: ACA0 plus Σ¹ₖ choice, resp. Σ¹ₖ dependent choice, resp. strong Σ¹ₖ dependent choice. Σ¹ₖ-IND is the induction scheme for Σ¹ₖ formulas.
statement.facts: Σ¹ₖ-AC0 implies ∆¹ₖ-CA0; Σ¹ₖ-DC0 implies Σ¹ₖ-AC0 and Σ¹ₖ-IND; strong Σ¹ₖ-DC0 implies Π¹ₖ-CA0 (Lemma VII.6.6). Σ¹₂-AC0 ≡ ∆¹₂-CA0, Σ¹₂-DC0 ≡ ∆¹₂-CA0 + Σ¹₂-IND, strong Σ¹₂-DC0 ≡ Π¹₂-CA0, and strong Σ¹₁-DC0 ≡ Π¹₁-CA0 (Theorem VII.6.9). Analogous equivalences hold for Σ¹ₖ₊₃ under ∃X∀Y(Y ∈ L(X)) (Theorem VII.6.16), with Π¹₄ conservation results (Theorem VII.6.20). Strength strictly increases: Σ¹ₖ₊₁-DC0 < strong Σ¹ₖ₊₁-DC0 < Σ¹ₖ₊₂-DC0 (Theorem VII.7.7).

statement.name: βk-model reflection for Σ1m formulas
statement.definition: Every Σ¹ₘ formula θ(X) that holds is satisfied in some countable coded βₖ-model containing X.
statement.facts: Strong Σ¹ₖ₊₁-DC0 is equivalent to the existence of a countable coded βₖ₊₁-model containing any given X (Theorem VII.7.4), and to βₖ₊₁-model reflection for Σ¹ₖ₊₃ formulas. Σ¹ₖ₊₂-DC0 is equivalent to βₖ₊₁-model reflection for Σ¹ₖ₊₄ formulas (Theorem VII.7.6).

statement.name: Set-theoretic counterparts of ATR0 and stronger L2 theories
statement.definition: Basic set theory with regularity, countability and Axiom Beta (existence of collapsing functions of regular relations), plus the axioms of T0.
statement.facts: ATR0^set is a conservative extension of ATR0, and more generally T0^set of T0 (Theorems VII.3.23, VII.3.34). Π¹₁-CA0^set proves the Shoenfield absoluteness theorem (Theorem VII.4.14).

statement.name: Lusin's separation theorem, Borel domain theorem, unique-paths scheme
statement.definition: Lusin: disjoint analytic sets are separated by a Borel set. Borel domain: the domain of a single-valued Borel relation is Borel. Unique paths: for a sequence of trees each with at most one path, the set of indices of trees with a path exists.
statement.facts: Lusin's theorem and the Borel domain theorem are provable in ATR0. The unique-paths scheme, also in its arithmetical-formula form, is equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem V.5.2). Souslin's theorem holds in HYP, so it is not equivalent to ATR0 (Remark V.3.12).

statement.name: Perfect set theorem
statement.definition: Every uncountable analytic set (equivalently, every closed set of 2^N or N^N with uncountably many paths) has a nonempty perfect subset.
statement.facts: All versions are equivalent to ATR0 over ACA0 (Theorem V.5.5).

statement.name: Σ11 axiom of choice
statement.definition: ∀k∃X φ(k,X) → ∃Y∀k φ(k,(Y)_k) for Σ11 formulas φ.
statement.facts: Provable in ATR0 (Theorem V.8.3). Not equivalent to ATR0: HYP satisfies it but not ATR0 (Remark V.8.4).

statement.name: Kondo's coanalytic uniformization theorem
statement.definition: Coanalytic relations on 2^N × 2^N can be uniformized by coanalytic relations.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π11-CA0 over ATR0 (Theorem VI.2.6).

statement.name: Π11 transfinite recursion; Σ11 monotonic induction
statement.definition: Π11-TR0 is ACA0 plus transfinite recursion along well orderings for Π11 formulas. Σ11-MI0 is Tanaka's system based on Σ11 monotonic induction.
statement.facts: Cited from Tanaka: Π11-TR0 is equivalent over RCA0 to Δ02 determinacy and to the Δ11 Ramsey theorem (Theorem VI.7.3). Σ11-MI0 is equivalent over RCA0 to Σ02 determinacy and to the Σ11 Ramsey theorem (Theorem VI.7.5).

statement.name: Weak Σ¹₁ choice
statement.definition: ACA0 plus ∀n(∃ exactly one Y)θ(n,Y) → ∃Z∀n θ(n,(Z)_n) for arithmetical θ.
statement.facts: Implied by Σ11-AC and (exercise) by Δ11-CA. Every countable coded ω-model of it is closed under hyperarithmetic reducibility. HYP is its minimum ω-model. For any recursive S ⊇ weak Σ11-AC0 with a countable ω-model, HYP is the intersection of all countable ω-models of S.

statement.name: ω-model reflection
statement.definition: ACA0 plus: every true (Σ1k) formula with set parameters holds in some countable coded ω-model of ACA0 containing the parameters.
statement.facts: Σ1∞-RFN0 is equivalent to Π1∞-TI0 (Thm VIII.5.4). Π11-TI0 ≡ Σ11-DC0 ≡ Σ13-RFN0 over ACA0 (Thm VIII.5.12). Π1∞-CA0 proves all instances. Essentially-Σ11 reflection is provable in ATR0 (Lemma VIII.6.3).

statement.name: Strong Π⁰₁ dependent choice
statement.definition: ∃Z∀n∀Y(η(n,(Z)^n,Y) → η(n,(Z)^n,(Z)_n)) for Π01 η.
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0. Used to show WKL0 proves the existence of countable coded strict β-models containing any X.

statement.name: Existence of H-sets (iterated jumps along well orderings)
statement.definition: For every X and every X-recursive well-ordering notation a, the jump hierarchy H^X_a exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over ACA0 (Theorem VIII.3.15).

statement.name: Existence of smallest weak-*-closed set/convex set/subspace containing a countable set
statement.definition: For every separable Banach space X and every countable Y ⊆ X*, there is a smallest weak-*-closed set (convex set, subspace) containing Y.
statement.facts: Each version, including those with X = c0, is equivalent to Π11-CA0 over RCA0 (cited from Humphreys/Simpson).

statement.name: König coverings for countable bipartite graphs
statement.definition: Every countable bipartite graph has a König covering.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (cited from Aharoni/Magidor/Shore and Simpson).

statement.name: Perfect matching theorems
statement.definition: Hall's condition characterizes perfect matchings in countable locally finite bipartite graphs; regular countable bipartite graphs have perfect matchings.
statement.facts: The Hall-type statements are equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0. The n-regular and 2-regular marriage theorems are equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (cited from Hirst).

statement.name: Dickson's lemma
statement.definition: For each m, N^m is well quasiordered.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to the well-orderedness of ω^ω. The Hilbert basis theorem is also equivalent to it (Remark X.3.21).

statement.name: Higman's theorem (wqo version)
statement.definition: If Q is a wqo, then Q^{<N} under embeddability is a wqo.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Minimal bad sequence lemma
statement.definition: Nash-Williams' minimal bad sequence lemma in wqo theory.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π11-CA0 over RCA0 (Marcone and Simpson).

statement.name: Dushnik–Miller theorem
statement.definition: Every countably infinite linear ordering has a nontrivial self-embedding.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Downey/Lempp).

statement.name: Jump hierarchy problem (Weihrauch version of ATR)
statement.definition: Given a well-ordering L and a set A, produce the jump hierarchy on L starting with A.
statement.facts: ATR is parallelizable (Prop 2.7). CWO ≡W ATR ≡W WCWO (Cor 2.31). ATR ≡W UC_{N^N} (cited from Kihara–Marcone–Pauly). ATR ≤W C_N ∗ NDS_WO and ATR ≤W C_N ∗ NIAC_WO (Thms 2.32, 2.33). ATR ≤W KDT (Thm 3.33). The catalogue's atr is the sentence ATR0, not this problem.

statement.name: Comparability / weak comparability of well-orderings
statement.definition: Given two well-orderings, produce an embedding of one onto an initial segment of (CWO), resp. into (WCWO), the other.
statement.facts: CWO ≡sW UC_{N^N} ≡sW ATR (cited). CWO ≡W ATR ≡W WCWO.

statement.name: Fraïssé's conjecture and restrictions
statement.definition: Given a sequence of linear orders (resp. well-orders), produce i<j with an embedding L_i → L_j; variants for descending sequences and antichains.
statement.facts: WQO_WO ≤W ATR. ATR ≤c NDS_WO and ATR ≤c NIAC_WO. UC_{N^N} <c WQO_LO <W C_{N^N}. C_{N^N} is not arithmetically Weihrauch reducible to WQO_LO. WQO_LO has a computable instance with no hyperarithmetic solution.

statement.name: Two-sided versions
statement.definition: As CWO/WCWO/ATR on arbitrary linear orders, with an infinite descending sequence also accepted as a solution.
statement.facts: UC_{N^N} <W P <W C_{N^N} for each of them. None is ≤c UC_{N^N}. Each has a computable instance with no hyperarithmetic solution. CWO2 ≤W ATR2.

statement.name: König's duality theorem
statement.definition: Given a countable bipartite graph, produce a König cover (C, M).
statement.facts: KDT ≤W C_{N^N}, while C_{N^N} is not arithmetically Weihrauch reducible to KDT. KDT is parallelizable. ATR ≤W KDT. ATR2 ≤W LPO ∗ KDT. KDT is arithmetically Weihrauch equivalent to ATR2. LPO ≤W KDT.

statement.name: Σ¹₁ axiom of finite choice
statement.definition: If for each n there are finitely many Y with φ(n, Y) (φ arithmetic), then there is a sequence (Z_n) with φ(n, Z_n) for all n.
statement.facts: ABW0 implies it over IΣ¹₁. It does not imply INDEC0, Δ¹₁-CA0 or Σ¹₁-AC0. There is an ω-model of Δ¹₁-CA not satisfying it, so neither Δ¹₁-CA0 nor unique-Σ¹₁-AC0 implies it.

statement.name: Arithmetic Bolzano–Weierstrass
statement.definition: An arithmetic predicate on 2^N has finitely many solutions or its solution set has an accumulation point.
statement.facts: Implies finite-Σ¹₁-AC0 over IΣ¹₁. There is an ω-model of ABW not satisfying IRT.

statement.name: (Weak) infinite ray theorem (Halin)
statement.definition: If a graph has k disjoint rays for each k (WIRT: given as a sequence of sets), then it has infinitely many disjoint rays.
statement.facts: ACA0 proves WIRT. RCA0 does not prove WIRT, even for highly recursive graphs. RCA0 proves WIRT for trees. Σ¹₁-AC0 proves IRT. IRT implies ACA0, and implies ABW0 over IΣ¹₁. IRT is a theorem of hyperarithmetic analysis. Nonuniform-WIRT is equivalent to ACA0.

statement.name: Theories of hyperarithmetic analysis
statement.definition: Σ¹₁ choice, Δ¹₁ comprehension, Σ¹₁ unique choice, and Jullien's indecomposability theorem.
statement.facts: There is an ω-model of Δ¹₁-CA not satisfying finite-Σ¹₁-AC.
